characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: The Technical Feasibility Strategy aims to demonstrate the viability of platform-neutral and fallback authentication methods for Danish digital identity. It controls the scope and focus of technical demonstrators, influencing the credibility and persuasiveness of the project's technical evidence. Success is measured by the robustness and security of the demonstrators, their adherence to open standards, and their ability to function in simulated public-sector environments. Key metrics include successful authentication rates, security audit scores, and positive feedback from technical stakeholders.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever strongly synergizes with the Procurement Influence Strategy (f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551). Credible technical demonstrators provide concrete evidence to support procurement requirements for platform neutrality and fallback access, making the advocacy more effective.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever has a potential conflict with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy (2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3). Focusing too narrowly on specific technical solutions may limit the project's ability to adapt to evolving EU standards and interoperability requirements.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: The Policy Advocacy Strategy focuses on shaping the policy landscape to favor platform-neutral and fallback-capable digital identity solutions. It controls the messaging and arguments used to influence Digitaliseringsstyrelsen, AltID planning, and related procurement decisions. Success is measured by the inclusion of platform-neutrality and fallback access requirements in official policy documents and procurement specifications. Key metrics include the number of formal engagements, the tone of responses, and the adoption of project recommendations.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever works in synergy with the Coalition Building Strategy (1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd). A broader coalition, encompassing diverse perspectives, strengthens the advocacy efforts and increases the likelihood of influencing policy decisions by presenting a united front.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever can conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474). Prioritizing certain policy arguments (e.g., open-source governance) might constrain the technical demonstrator work, making it harder to showcase a wider range of feasible solutions.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: The Coalition Building Strategy aims to create a broad base of support for platform-neutral digital identity in Denmark. It controls the scope and composition of the advocacy coalition, with the objective of increasing political pressure for change. Success is measured by the size and diversity of the coalition, the level of engagement from key stakeholders, and the coalition's ability to influence policy discussions. A strong coalition translates to a more powerful advocacy position in procurement and standards discussions.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever strongly enhances the Policy Advocacy Strategy (80b177d0). A larger, more diverse coalition provides a stronger voice and broader reach for policy proposals. It also supports the Procurement Influence Strategy (f1c0d856) by creating a more favorable political climate.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: A broad coalition can create internal conflicts, hindering the EU Standards Engagement Strategy (2e9016aa) if different groups prioritize conflicting standards. Focusing too narrowly on specific stakeholders may limit the overall reach and impact, conflicting with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39) if key technical voices are excluded.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: The Procurement Influence Strategy focuses on incorporating platform-neutrality and fallback access requirements into Danish digital identity procurement processes, particularly AltID. It controls the specificity of these requirements, aiming to reduce long-term dependency on Apple and Google. Success is measured by the inclusion of relevant language in procurement documents and the resulting supplier diversity. This lever directly impacts the design and implementation of future digital identity systems.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever works in synergy with the Policy Advocacy Strategy (80b177d0). Strong policy advocacy creates a favorable environment for including platform-neutral language in procurement. It also benefits from the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39), which provides evidence to support specific procurement requirements.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Focusing too narrowly on specific requirements may conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39) if those requirements prove technically challenging or expensive to implement. It may also conflict with the Coalition Building Strategy (1731ad9a) if overly strict requirements alienate potential vendors or stakeholders.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: The EU Standards Engagement Strategy focuses on influencing European digital identity standards, particularly within the European Digital Identity Wallet framework. It aims to align Danish advocacy with broader European requirements on interoperability, portability, resilience, and reduced platform lock-in. Success is measured by the inclusion of platform-neutrality, fallback access, continuity, resilience, or supplier-concentration language in relevant European Digital Identity Wallet materials. This lever directly impacts the long-term viability and scalability of platform-neutral digital identity solutions.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever strongly synergizes with the `Procurement Influence Strategy`, as EU standards can inform and strengthen Danish procurement requirements. It also benefits from the `Coalition Building Strategy`, as a broader coalition can amplify the project's voice within EU standards bodies.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever may conflict with the `Policy Advocacy Strategy` if EU-level goals diverge from immediate Danish policy priorities. It also competes for resources with the `Technical Feasibility Strategy` if extensive EU engagement detracts from demonstrator development.
